chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Hanan, from Shu'ayb who said:

We hired a group of workers for Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to work in his garden, and their term was until the afternoon prayer. He said, so when they finished, he said to Mu'ttab, 'Give them their wages before their sweat dries.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the timing of paying workers' wages according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on leases (Bab al-Ijarat) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Sunnah of immediate wage payment, using the vivid metaphor of 'before sweat dries' to emphasize urgency and prevent exploitation. It underscores the Imam’s practical application of justice in economic transactions, serving as a foundational precedent for the Islamic legal principle that wages are due upon completion of work unless a specific deferment was agreed upon.
